subject: Multi-stage onboarding & tranches for Dedicated GPU commitment - EdenAI
messages:
From: Hannah Mitchell <hannah@edenai.ai>
To: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity needs and preferred onboarding cadence

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the intro call earlier — EdenAI is excited about partnering with Redwood for inference. Our immediate ask is straightforward: we need a proposal that lays out a pragmatic path to reserved GPU capacity tied to our growth milestones. Key constraints:

- Q3 target: sustained 20k tokens/sec across our production endpoint (real-time chat).
- Budget envelope: capped monthly spend for the first 6 months while we prove latency SLAs.
- Security: VPC peering + customer KMS required.

Can you send a document that outlines 2–3 commitment tranches (minimum guaranteed GPUs, cluster topology, expected ramp weeks, bursting strategy, and fallbacks) and a suggested onboarding timeline we can share with procurement?

Attaching our 7-day sample usage and a short SRE note on traffic patterns.

Thanks,
Hannah Mitchell
Head of Platform Operations
EdenAI

Attachments: EdenAI_usage_sample.csv (CSV, 72KB)

From: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Mitchell <hannah@edenai.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-04T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity needs and preferred onboarding cadence

Hi Hannah — great speaking with you. I pulled together three pragmatic paths (attached PDF) so procurement has clear options. High level summary below — will follow up with a brief walk-through.

Option A — Proof stage (entry)
- Reserved minimum: 8x A100-equivalent GPUs (single AZ)
- Purpose: validate production integration and latency SLOs with canary traffic (~10% of prod)
- Ramp: 2 weeks to full ingress for canary; 6-week review to decide next tranche
- Burst: can use hosted overflow up to +50% at higher unit cost
- Use cases: integration, end-to-end latency validation

Option B — Scale tranche (production)
- Reserved minimum: 24x GPUs (2 AZ spread, sticky routing)
- Purpose: support peak sustained throughput target for early production (50–60% of Q3 target)
- Ramp: staged 4-week ramp (staging -> perf -> canary -> cutover)
- Burst: configurable shared pool bursting to 40 GPUs; autoscaling policy to preserve latency SLOs

Option C — Enterprise reserve (commitment)
- Reserved minimum: 64x GPUs (multi-region standby + primary cluster)
- Purpose: full Q3 capacity with predictable unit economics and SLA (SLA for <100ms p95 on your vector infra pattern)
- Ramp: phased onboarding over 8–12 weeks with training windows and traffic shaping; includes two canary rollouts, regression evals, and fallback policy to a smaller model variant on overload
- Extra: dedicated on-call + extended observability retention (30d)

Attachments: Redwood proposal PDF contains detailed burn-rate estimates, pricing tiers, staging checklist, and required network/KMS configuration.

If this looks good, Ben can prepare a commercial term sheet and I'll sync with our provisioning team on the earliest start date.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: EdenAI_Dedicated_Options_Q2.pdf (PDF, 420KB)

From: Hannah Mitchell <hannah@edenai.ai>
To: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-04T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity needs and preferred onboarding cadence

Thanks Monica — this is exactly what procurement asked for. A couple quick clarifications before we loop legal:

1) For Option B, can you explicitly call out the minimum guaranteed GPUs during business hours vs. off-hours (we expect a nightly drop to ~30% of peak)?
2) For bursting, what is the typical latency penalty and can you guarantee no cold-starts when burst capacity is consumed?

Also — can you add an explicit rollback runbook if a model regression appears after cutover? Procurement wants a short SLA paragraph.

I can setup a procurement + SRE call next Tuesday 10am PT if that works for you.

— Hannah

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Mitchell <hannah@edenai.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-05T09:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity needs and preferred onboarding cadence

Hannah — good questions. Quick answers and we'll expand in the next doc updates: 

• Minimum guarantee (Option B): we can define a time-windowed guarantee. Example: 24 GPUs guaranteed during 07:00–19:00 PT (business hours), and 12 GPUs guaranteed overnight. Billing/pricing reflects those windows and is itemized in the commercial term sheet.

• Bursting behavior: when bursting into the shared pool, there is typically a 10–35ms tail latency increase depending on request mix; we mitigate cold-starts via pre-warmed placements and predictive KV cache warming. For strict no-cold-start SLAs we recommend Option C or a warm idle pool.

• Rollback runbook: we'll include an automated canary rollback (traffic-split reversal), model pinning to previous version, and an ops-runbook that calls out telemetry thresholds (p95 latency, error-rate change >2x, BLEU/LL metrics delta). We'll attach the short runbook to the term sheet.

If Tuesday 10am PT works, we can have engineering (Aditya) and finance on the call to confirm timelines and pricing buckets.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Mitchell <hannah@edenai.ai>
To: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-06T16:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity needs and preferred onboarding cadence

Tuesday 10am PT works for us — scheduling now. Please include: procurement lead (L. Chen), a short PDF with the time-windowed guarantees and explicit rollback runbook, and an updated cost table that shows both flat monthly vs. windowed-guarantee pricing so we can fast-track procurement.

I'll share the calendar invite and include a short procurement checklist so we can close the PO quickly. Looking forward to the call.

Best,
Hannah Mitchell
Head of Platform Operations
EdenAI

Forwarded-attachments: EdenAI_Dedicated_Options_Q2.pdf
